literal: Soon he was removed as Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed as Marquis of Chiyang county.
idiomatic: Before long he was relieved of attendant-in-ordinary and enfeoffed as marquis of Chiyang county.

literal: Seeing Emperor Wenxuan's edicts grow ever stricter, he sought to leave office; he was appointed Inspector of Zhao province, yet never took up the post and remained a court jester.
idiomatic: When he saw Emperor Wenxuan's rule turning harsh he asked to leave the capital. He was made inspector of Zhao province but never took up the post and remained a court buffoon.

literal: In Huangjian year 2 he was appointed Inspector of Western Yan province.
idiomatic: In the second year of Huangjian he was appointed inspector of Western Yan province.

literal: Before he took office, Empress Dowager Wuming fell ill; Zhicai treated her and she recovered at once; Emperor Xiaozhao gave a thousand rolls of colored silk and four hundred bolts of brocade.
idiomatic: He had not yet gone to his post when Empress Dowager Wuming fell ill. Zhicai treated her and she recovered at once. Emperor Xiaozhao rewarded him with a thousand rolls of silk and four hundred bolts of brocade.

literal: Zhicai being skilled in medicine, though given an external appointment, he was soon recalled.
idiomatic: Because his medical skill was outstanding, though he was granted an outside post he was recalled within a short time.

literal: Being broadly learned and well informed, he became especially adept in the arts of occult calculation.
idiomatic: He was widely read and well informed, and on that account became especially skilled in prognostication and the occult arts.

literal: In spring of the second year of Daning, Empress Dowager Wuming fell ill again.
idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Daning the empress dowager Wuming fell ill again.

literal: Zhicai's younger brother Zhifan was Director of the Imperial Pharmacy; he was ordered to examine and attend her.
idiomatic: Zhicai's younger brother Zhifan was director of the imperial pharmacy and was ordered to examine and treat her.

literal: The inner officials all ordered that the empress dowager be called Stone Granny; there was a popular taboo, so they changed her name to ward it off.
idiomatic: The inner officials all had the empress dowager addressed as "Stone Granny," a folk taboo-name meant to turn aside misfortune.

literal: Zhifan came out and told Zhicai, "A children's rhyme runs: 'Within Zhou, Qiqiu Jia; at Leopard Shrine a bride for Stone Granny; Cut-grave as matchmaker—only a measure of purple silk boots.'"
idiomatic: Zhifan came out and told Zhicai, "A children's rhyme says: 'Within Zhou, Qiqiu Jia; at Leopard Shrine they wed Stone Granny; Cut-grave serves as matchmaker—you get only a measure of purple silk boots.'"

literal: Now the empress dowager has suddenly had her name changed—this is a private act that invites the strange."
idiomatic: "Now the empress dowager has suddenly been renamed—that is a private act that invites ill omens."

literal: Zhicai said, "Qiqiu Jia—in Hu speech, 'already gone.'"
idiomatic: Zhicai said, "'Qiqiu Jia' is Hu speech for 'already gone.'"

literal: "Leopard Shrine weds Stone Granny—can that be anything good?"
idiomatic: "'Leopard Shrine weds Stone Granny'—can that portend anything good?"

literal: "Cut-grave as matchmaker—only let joint burial come from Cut-grave."
idiomatic: "'Cut-grave as matchmaker'—read it as joint burial arising from the grave."

literal: "'Only purple silk boots'—she will reach the fourth month; how so?"
idiomatic: "'Only a measure of purple silk boots'—she will reach the fourth month. How do I know?"

literal: "The character for purple is 'this' with 'thread' beneath; 'extended' means ripe—it should fall within the fourth month."
idiomatic: "The character for purple is 'this' with 'thread' below; 'extended' means ripe. The omen falls in the middle of the fourth month."

literal: Zhifan asked what the boots meant.
idiomatic: Zhifan asked what the boots signified.

literal: Zhicai said, "Boots—beside leather stands 'transform'; how could they be a lasting thing?"
idiomatic: Zhicai said, "Boots: beside 'leather' stands 'transform.' How could that be something that lasts?"

literal: On the first day of the fourth month the empress dowager indeed died.
idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month the empress dowager died, just as he had said.

literal: Someone suffered swollen, painful heels; no physician could identify the ailment.
idiomatic: A man suffered swollen, painful heels, and no physician could name the disease.

literal: Zhicai said, "It is clam-spirit sickness, from taking a boat to sea and letting his feet hang in the water."
idiomatic: Zhicai said, "This is clam-spirit sickness, contracted by sailing the sea and dangling his feet in the water."

literal: The patient said, "That is indeed what happened."
idiomatic: The patient said, "That is exactly what I did."

literal: Zhicai cut him open and removed two clam embryos, each as large as an elm pod.
idiomatic: Zhicai cut him open and took out two clam embryos, each as large as an elm pod.

literal: Another man used bone for a knife handle, five-colored and variegated.
idiomatic: Another man had made a knife handle from bone, five-colored and streaked.

literal: Zhicai said, "This man has a tumor."
idiomatic: Zhicai said, "This man has a tumor."

literal: Asked where he had got it, he said that in an ancient tomb he had seen a skull whose forehead bone was several inches long; he tried shaving it and found a grain, so he used it.
idiomatic: Asked where he had found it, he said that in an old tomb he had seen a skull whose forehead bone was several inches long; he shaved it and found a grain in the bone, so he used it.

literal: His keen insight and wide mastery were like this.
idiomatic: His keen insight and wide mastery ran to such cases.

literal: In the fourth year of Tiantong he was promoted in succession to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; soon he was made Inspector of Yan province, with a special grant of one set of drums and pipes.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiantong he rose in steps to left vice director of the imperial secretariat, then was made inspector of Yan province with a special grant of one suite of drums and pipes.

literal: Zhicai's medical skill was supreme, and he alone was repeatedly summoned by imperial order.
idiomatic: Zhicai's medical skill stood above all others, and he alone was repeatedly summoned by imperial order.

literal: Emperor Wucheng indulged wine and women to excess and was often dazed and unsteady; once when his illness flared he himself said that at first he saw a five-colored thing in the air; as it drew nearer it turned into a beautiful woman standing several zhang above the ground, upright and poised.
idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng indulged wine and women beyond measure and was often dazed and unsteady. Once when his illness flared he said that at first he saw a five-colored thing in the air; as it drew nearer it became a beautiful woman standing several zhang above the ground, upright and still.

literal: After the time it takes to eat, it turned into Guanyin.
idiomatic: After the time it takes to eat a meal it turned into Guanyin.

literal: Zhicai said, "This comes from excessive lust and great depletion of the vital principle."
idiomatic: Zhicai said, "This comes from excessive lust and great depletion of the vital principle."

literal: He immediately prepared a decoction; after one dose the vision drew somewhat farther off; after another dose it turned back into a five-colored thing; after several doses of the broth the illness was wholly cured.
idiomatic: He immediately prepared a decoction. After one dose the vision drew farther away; after another it turned back into a five-colored thing; after several doses the illness was wholly cured.

literal: Whenever the emperor's illness flared he would send horsemen in pursuit of Zhicai; needles and drugs applied at once always took effect, so there were frequent occasions when Zhicai stood in attendance at the bedside.
idiomatic: Whenever the emperor's illness flared he sent riders to fetch Zhicai; needles and drugs applied on the spot always worked at once, so Zhicai was often kept in attendance at the bedside.

literal: When autumn came Emperor Wucheng grew somewhat settled and no longer suffered flare-ups.
idiomatic: When autumn came Emperor Wucheng grew somewhat settled and no longer suffered flare-ups.

literal: He Shikai wished to advance in regular order; because Zhicai's household register was attached to Yan province, which was his native jurisdiction, he memorialized that Zhicai be additionally appointed inspector there, with Hu Changren as Left Vice Director and He Shikai as Right Vice Director.
idiomatic: He Shikai wished to advance in regular order. Because Zhicai's household register was attached to Yan province, which was his home jurisdiction, he memorialized that Zhicai be sent out as inspector there, with Hu Changren as left vice director and He Shikai as right vice director.

literal: In the tenth month the emperor's illness flared again; he told He Shikai, "I regret sending Zhicai out on an external post—it has made me suffer."
idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor's illness flared again. He told He Shikai, "I regret sending Zhicai out to a provincial post—it has made me suffer."

literal: On the eighth day of that month an edict went out by post relay to recall Zhicai.
idiomatic: On the eighth day of that month an edict went out by post relay to recall Zhicai.

literal: The emperor died on the tenth; Zhicai did not arrive until the eleventh.
idiomatic: The emperor died on the tenth; Zhicai did not arrive until the eleventh.

literal: There was nothing left to do; he returned to take up his provincial post.
idiomatic: There was nothing left for him to do, and he returned to his provincial post.

literal: In office he committed no oppression or violence, but he was not very versed in law and was rather negligent and casual, doing as he pleased in appointments and dismissals.
idiomatic: In office he committed no oppression or violence, but he was not well versed in law and was rather negligent and casual, appointing and dismissing as he pleased.

literal: In the winter of the fifth year the Last Ruler summoned Zhicai.
idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year the last ruler summoned Zhicai.

literal: Soon the left vice directorship fell vacant; Zhicai said, "I can surely repeat Yu's achievement."
idiomatic: Soon the left vice directorship fell vacant. Zhicai said, "Surely I can repeat Yu's achievement."

literal: In the first year of Wuping he was again appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping he was again appointed left vice director of the imperial secretariat.

literal: Zhicai toward He Shikai and Lu Lingxuan mother and son was utterly obsequious and familiar; when the two households fell gravely ill he contrived a hundred ways to save them.
idiomatic: Toward He Shikai and Lu Lingxuan, mother and son, Zhicai was utterly obsequious and familiar; when the two households fell gravely ill he contrived a hundred ways to save them.

literal: On that account he was promoted to Director of the Imperial Secretariat and enfeoffed as Prince of Xiyang commandery.
idiomatic: On that account he was promoted to director of the imperial secretariat and enfeoffed as prince of Xiyang commandery.

literal: When Zu Ting held power he appointed Zhicai Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: When Zu Ting held power he appointed Zhicai attendant-in-ordinary and grand tutor of the heir apparent.

literal: Zhicai said resentfully, "Ziye has winnowed me out."
idiomatic: Zhicai said resentfully, "Ziye has winnowed me out."

literal: Ting had an eye ailment, so he was compared to Music Master Kuang.
idiomatic: Ting suffered from an eye ailment, so Zhicai compared him to Music Master Kuang.

literal: Zhicai was clever in debate and had a strong memory, with more than ordinary quickness; he especially loved witty talk and raillery, and in public and private gatherings people often mocked one another in sport.
idiomatic: Zhicai was clever in debate and had a strong memory, with more than ordinary quickness. He especially loved witty talk and raillery; at public and private gatherings people often mocked one another in sport.

literal: Zheng Daoyu often jested that Zhicai was Master-and-Duke.
idiomatic: Zheng Daoyu often jested that Zhicai was "Master-and-Duke."

literal: Zhicai said, "Since I am your teacher and also your duke, in the Three Bonds I suddenly hold two of the roles."
idiomatic: Zhicai said, "Since I am your teacher and also your duke, among the Three Bonds I suddenly hold two of the roles."

literal: He also mocked Wang Xin's surname: "With speech it is the 'speech' radical plus king; near a dog it becomes 'mad'; add a neck and legs and it is 'horse'; put horns and a tail and it is 'sheep.'"
idiomatic: He also mocked Wang Xin's surname: "Add speech and you get the character wang; put it near a dog and it becomes 'mad'; add neck and legs and it is 'horse'; put on horns and a tail and it is 'sheep.'"

literal: Lu Yuanming jested with Zhicai, "Your surname is 'not yet entered among men'; your given name is a mistaken character—'zhi' should be 'fa' (lack)."
idiomatic: Lu Yuanming jested with Zhicai, "Your surname is 'not yet entered among men'; your given name is a mistaken character—'zhi' should be 'fa' (lack)."

literal: He answered at once, "Your surname with 'death' added is 'tyrant'; on a mound it is 'void'; if you bear a son he is a 'captive'; if you raise a horse it is an 'ass.'"
idiomatic: He answered at once, "Your surname with 'death' added is 'tyrant'; on a mound it is 'void'; if you bear a son he is a 'captive'; if you raise a horse it is an 'ass.'"

literal: He also once went out with court gentlemen; from afar they saw a pack of dogs racing.
idiomatic: He also once went out with court gentlemen and from afar saw a pack of dogs racing.

literal: The others tried to have him name them on sight; Zhicai answered at once, "Are they Song Que, or Han Lu—or chasing Li Si eastward, or carrying the Emperor's Daughter south?"
idiomatic: The others asked him to name them on sight. Zhicai answered at once, "Are they Song Que or Han Lu—or chasing Li Si eastward, or carrying the Emperor's Daughter south?"

literal: Li He at a great gathering invoked his father's name and said, "Do you like raw bear's paw?"
idiomatic: At a great gathering Li He invoked his father's name and said, "Do you like raw bear's paw?"

literal: Zhicai said, "So-so."
idiomatic: Zhicai said, "So-so."

literal: He also said, "Is what you said logically fair?"
idiomatic: He also said, "Is what you said logically fair?"

literal: He fled at once to avoid him; on the road he met his nephew Gao Dezheng.
idiomatic: He fled at once to avoid him. On the road he met his nephew Gao Dezheng.

literal: Dezheng said, "Uncle, why is your face not pleased?"
idiomatic: Dezheng said, "Uncle, why do you look displeased?"

literal: He told him the reason.
idiomatic: He told him the reason.

literal: Dezheng went straight to the seat and repeatedly demanded bear's paw.
idiomatic: Dezheng went straight to the gathering and repeatedly demanded bear's paw.

literal: Zhicai said to those seated, "Whose taboo is it?"
idiomatic: Zhicai said to those seated, "Whose taboo is it?"

literal: No one knew.
idiomatic: No one knew.

literal: Zhicai said, "Alive he was unknown to others; dead he is not tabooed to others—why should that be worth asking?"
idiomatic: Zhicai said, "Alive he was unknown to others; dead he is not tabooed to others—why is that worth asking?"

literal: Tang Yong and Bai Jian were then in high favor; people said, "In Bingzhou, Tang and Bai blaze bright."
idiomatic: Tang Yong and Bai Jian were then in high favor; people said, "In Bingzhou, Tang and Bai blaze bright."

literal: Zhicai despised them.
idiomatic: Zhicai despised them.

literal: On New Year's Day, facing Yong, he said to the clerks in blessing, "May you gentlemen in rank become Tang and Bai."
idiomatic: On New Year's Day, facing Yong, he said to the clerks in blessing, "May you gentlemen in rank become Tang and Bai."

literal: Because a junior clerk liked to chew his brush, he once held the tube to Yuan Wenyao's mouth and said, "Lend me your teeth."
idiomatic: Because a junior clerk liked to chew his brush, he once held the tube to Yuan Wenyao's mouth and said, "Lend me your teeth."

literal: His insolence was like this.
idiomatic: His insolence ran to such lengths.

literal: Serving several emperors, he won favor through jesting familiarity.
idiomatic: Serving several emperors, he won favor through jesting familiarity.

literal: Emperor Wucheng had buck teeth; he asked the physicians.
idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng had buck teeth and asked the physicians about them.

literal: Director of the Imperial Pharmacy Deng Xuanwen answered truthfully; Wucheng in anger had him flogged.
idiomatic: Director of the imperial pharmacy Deng Xuanwen answered truthfully; Wucheng in anger had him flogged.

literal: Later he asked Zhicai, who bowed in congratulation and said, "These are wisdom teeth; one who grows wisdom teeth is clever and long-lived."
idiomatic: Later he asked Zhicai, who bowed in congratulation and said, "These are wisdom teeth; one who grows wisdom teeth is clever and long-lived."

literal: Wucheng was pleased and rewarded him.
idiomatic: Wucheng was pleased and rewarded him.

literal: When he was vice director he said to people, "In the southeast I saw Xu Mian serve as vice director, and no court gentleman failed to flatter him.
idiomatic: When he was vice director he told people, "In the southeast I saw Xu Mian serve as vice director, and no court gentleman failed to flatter him.

literal: Now I too am Vice Director Xu—yet not one person flatters me. How am I to live!"
idiomatic: Now I too am Vice Director Xu—yet not one person flatters me. How am I to live!"

literal: Zhicai's wife was a sister of the Prince of Guangyang of Wei; Zhicai had obtained her as wife through Gao Cheng.
idiomatic: Zhicai's wife was a sister of the prince of Guangyang of Wei; Zhicai had obtained her as wife through Gao Cheng.

literal: He Shikai learned of this and violated his wife.
idiomatic: He Shikai learned of this and violated his wife.

literal: Zhicai happened upon them and avoided them; he withdrew and said, "I am hindering the young man's sport."
idiomatic: Zhicai happened upon them and avoided them. He withdrew and said, "I am hindering the young man's sport."

literal: His indulgence was like this.
idiomatic: His indulgence ran to such lengths.

literal: He died at the age of eighty.
idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

literal: He was posthumously made Duke of the State of Situ and Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous title Civil and Bright.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made duke of the state of Situ and recorder of affairs of the imperial secretariat, with the posthumous title Civil and Bright.

literal: The eldest son Lin, style name Shaoqing, was a marshal of the Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: The eldest son Lin, style Shaoqing, was marshal of the grand commandant.

literal: The second son Tongqing was a household attendant of the heir apparent; Zhicai, because he had no learning, often sighed and said, "In the end I fear he will share the fate of the Guangling melody."
idiomatic: The second son Tongqing was a household attendant of the heir apparent. Because Tongqing had no learning, Zhicai often sighed and said, "In the end I fear he will share the fate of the Guangling melody."

literal: The younger brother Zhifan was also known for medical skill; he reached Minister of Ceremonies and was specially permitted to inherit Zhicai's title as Prince of Xiyang.
idiomatic: His younger brother Zhifan was also known for medical skill. He reached minister of ceremonies and was specially permitted to inherit Zhicai's title as prince of Xiyang.

literal: After entering Zhou he was appointed General of the Household with Insignia Equal to Three Offices.
idiomatic: After entering Zhou he was appointed general of the household with insignia equal to three offices.

literal: He died in the Kaihuang era.
idiomatic: He died in the Kaihuang era.

literal: The complete text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
